manifest.title: fun-lab: slug and default display name

contract.summary: The two string transforms laravel-fun-lab borrows from Laravel and every twin must reproduce: the slug a catalog entity is stored under (Str::slug) and the display name it gets when none is given (Str::headline). An entity set up under 'First Login' in one runtime has to be found under the same slug in another, or a shared catalog splits in two.

functions.slug: slug(value: string) -> string - lowercase, separator '-', ASCII-folded, '@' spelled 'at', runs of separators collapsed and trimmed.
functions.headline: headline(value: string) -> string - words split on spaces, '-', '_' and case changes, each capitalised, joined with one space.

contract.referenceNote: Goldens are Illuminate\Support\Str::slug and Str::headline as installed in laravel-fun-lab's dev dependencies, written by laravel-fun-lab/tests/Conformance/ExportFixturesTest.php. Inputs are authored in fancy-conformance/scripts/fun-lab/strings.input.json.

cases.title: a slug is its own slug
words are lowercased and joined with '-'
underscores become the separator
cases.notes: Str::slug turns '_' into '-'. A twin that keeps underscores stores a second entity for the same name.

cases.title: '@' is spelled 'at'
cases.notes: Laravel's default dictionary replaces '@' with '-at-' before folding. Easy to miss and invisible until two runtimes disagree.

cases.title: punctuation other than separators is dropped
a camel-case word is lowercased, not split
cases.notes: slug does NOT split on case changes (headline does). The pair 0010/0020 catches a twin that reuses one word-splitter for both.

cases.title: an empty string is an empty slug
a CJK-only value slugs to the empty string
cases.notes: Str::slug with the default 'en' language drops CJK rather than transliterating it, so a catalog entity named only in a non-Latin script gets an empty slug. A twin that 'helpfully' transliterates, or keeps the characters, stores it under a slug PHP can never find.

cases.title: an all-caps word is lowercased after its first letter
cases.notes: Str::headline('Combat XP') is 'Combat Xp', and it is what setup() names an entity set up under 'Combat XP' with no name. Surprising, and pinned so no twin 'fixes' it alone: a twin answering 'Combat XP' shows a different name for the same catalog row.

cases.title: digits stay attached to their word
repeated separators do not make empty words
